firstPlayerRule: In standard multiplayer play, whoever can make the most amazing animal noise goes first.
houseFallback: If your group cannot agree on an animal noise or prefers another approach, agree to choose randomly. This is this site’s suggested house rule.
clarifications: Give that player the snow leopard. After Preparation, its holder takes the first Adapting turn and later begins the clockwise Feeding turns.
After scoring a non-final round, pass the snow leopard to the left before the next round’s Preparation.
The Quick Play variant makes Adapting simultaneous; the five- and six-player rules use that variant. The snow leopard still identifies who starts Feeding.

internalEvidence: Complete publisher-hosted or publisher-linked PDF retrieved; relevant setup, opening-turn, variant and edition pages read and visually inspected. Reviewed PDF pages: 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 13. Rendered spread 3 selects the most amazing animal noise. Spreads 4–6 distinguish common Preparation from the sequential default Adapting turns, beginning with the snow leopard holder; the shared Trait reveal happens after those turns. Spread 8 confirms clockwise Feeding starts with that holder. Spread 10 rotates the marker left after scoring and separately describes simultaneous Adapting in Quick Play and five/six-player games. Credits identify Dominic Crapuchettes's NorthStar game, matching inventory identity 330152, not Renature. The December 2025 filename is not treated as an explicit printing date.
